cohort: 1,297,037 pregnant and puerperal women in Denmark
finding: Significant risk factors for venous thromboembolism during pregnancy or the puerperal period included hospitalization, infection, hyperemesis, multiple pregnancies, preeclampsia, obesity, cesarean section, major postpartum bleeding, and intrauterine growth restriction or fetal death.
mod_finding: Elective and acute cesarean sections were associated with increased incidence rates of venous thromboembolism (23.2 and 34.0 per 10,000 women years, respectively).
